item.title: Fire & Safety Inspection Services for DVPHA housing
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $48K | Vendor: Pyramid Safety & Health Solutions Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Pyramid Safety & Health Solutions Inc a $47,760 contract, through a small purchase from a certified minority- or women-owned business without competition, for fire safety inspections of licensed family-type and foster family care homes for adults from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2029.

The Adult Protective Services (APS) Division of Voluntary and Proprietary Homes for Adults (DVPHA), which operates two state-mandated housing programs that utilize private housing as licensed residences. They are the Family-type Homes for Adults (FTHA) and the Foster Family Care Program (FFCP). Fire safety inspections for homes used by these programs are required by New York State regulations concerning eligibility for an operating license. The New York City Human Resources Administration and Adult Protective services have the responsibility for supervision of these programs. The lowest bidder, Pyramid Safety and Health Solution, Inc is our current vendor. They have been providing fire and safety inspection services to the clients over six (6) years. They are very responsive and responsible to the program. Their bid price is fair and reasonable. Contract budget: $47,760 Contract term: 7/1/2026 - 6/30/2029 PIN: 26ZSEAP01101

item.title: FY27 NAE - Scatter Site Housing (60 units)
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $3.3M | Vendor: Harlem Congregations for Community Improvement Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Harlem Congregations for Community Improvement Inc. a $3,321,945 one-year negotiated extension, with a 25% allowance, to continue permanent housing and supportive services for 60 scatter-site units for HASA clients until new contracts are awarded.

In accordance with PPB Rule Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii), the HRA/HASA is requesting a one-year Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE with a 25% allowance included for the Harlem Congregations for Community Improvement, Inc.s (HCCI) contract for 60 scatter site units. This contract provides permanent housing and supportive services to HASA clients. This NAE with HCCI is to maintain continuity of shelter services for HASA clients for the minimum amount of time until new RFP awards are processed. Prior to utilizing the NAE method, DHS exhausted both Renewal and Extensions for this contract. The incumbent vendor has been providing the services in accordance with the contract terms, and the performance has been satisfactory.

item.title: Support SAN Switches for 1 year
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $67K | Vendor: Abrahams Consulting LLC In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Abrahams Consulting LLC a $67,494 one-year contract for support of its SAN storage switches, using a noncompetitive small purchase from a certified minority- or women-owned business.

The Agencys current SAN Storage Brocade Switches are no longer under maintenance support, meaning the vendor will not provide software updates, security patches, technical support, or hardware replacements for this model. This situation poses a significant risk and has the potential to impact our business operations, as 100% of the Agencys production environment relies on these Brocade switches. To mitigate this risk, it is crucial for DSS ITS to secure break-fix support to ensure that our mission-critical enterprise applications remain operational. To maintain confidence in our ability to perform quick repairs and provide tracking reports and uptime for production we need this procurement as soon as possible.

item.title: 26SSEIT22001-Subscription of 3 Consumer Data Statara Licenses
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $99K | Vendor: Compulink Technologies Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Compulink Technologies Inc a $99,495 contract, without open competition as a minority- or women-owned small business, to subscribe to three licenses for the Statara consumer dataset, which the notice says helps the city reach underserved New Yorkers during emergencies.

The Statara consumer dataset provides information on over 5.5 million adult New Yorkers. This serves as a single data source that provides far broader coverage than PEU can get from various partner agency sources. Having this broad coverage is critical during emergencies and also helps PEU reach New Yorkers who have fewer existing touchpoints with the City. Without the consumer file in question, PEUs efforts to reach out to underserved New Yorkers, especially during and after emergencies, will be greatly impaired. This procurement is therefore necessary for continuation of critical agency functions, a Mayoral Priority, and directly related to public health and safety. An annual license for a consumer detail analytics file install, including updated and refreshed cell phone contact data available for NYC to house in your internal analytics database. This will include NYC residents that may be overlooked on traditional publicly available and privately sourced data sets. An annual license for consumer details to house inside of your separately licensed CRM database.

item.title: 6 Month NAE with Safe Horizon Inc. for CVAP
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-09-21 In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration intends to extend its contract with Safe Horizon Inc. for six months, from Jan. 1 through June 30, 2027, for $9,527,801.88 to continue the Crime Victims Advocate Program.

On behalf of the Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV), the Department Social Services (DSS) intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) contract with Safe Horizon, Inc. to extend the contract for the Crime Victims Advocate Program (CVAP) by 6 months. CVAP places victim advocates for survivors of domestic violence and additional advocates for victims of every other category of crime in precincts and Housing Police Service Areas citywide. Advocates provide supportive counseling, connections to individual or group therapy, and help navigating the legal and financial challenges that can emerge after a crime has occurred. CVAP represents the Citys largest single investment in supportive services for victims of crime and regularly reaches more than 40,000 crime victims annually.

The proposed NAE term will be from 1/1/2027 through 6/30/2027 with a contract amount of $9,527,801.88.

Procurement and award are in accordance with PPB Rule Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) for the reasons set forth herein.

item.title: Case Management Services - Staten Island
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $500K | Vendor: Caring Homes for the Homeless Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Caring Homes for the Homeless Inc a $500,000 contract, chosen from competing proposals from a pre-qualified list, to provide emergency case management to Staten Island disaster survivors.

DSS/HRA goals  are to provide emergency and on-call case management services to victims affected by a large-scale disaster or other emergencies. Case managers would facilitate the delivery of appropriate resources and services. The selected proposers would work with disaster survivors to develop and carry out a client-specific recovery plan with the goal of stabilization and a return to normalcy. This partnership would facilitate client access to a range of resources. The services to be provided may include an assessment of the client verified disaster-caused unmet needs; development of a goal-oriented plan; organization and coordination of information on available resources; monitoring progress toward reaching the recovery plan goals; and, when necessary, client advocacy. Competition pool 5 Staten Island
